name: Westslope cutthroat trout
note: Threatened (federal SARA). Native to the Bow and Oldman drainages. Catch-and-release in nearly all eastern-slopes waters.

name: Bull trout
note: Alberta's provincial fish. Catch-and-release province-wide. Tell it from brook trout: no black markings on the dorsal fin.

name: Athabasca rainbow trout
note: Native only to the upper Athabasca drainage (McLeod, Berland, Wildhay, Embarras and tributaries). Threatened. Catch-and-release in most of its range.

name: Arctic grayling
note: Native in the Athabasca, Smoky and Peace drainages near Grande Cache and Hinton. Stocked in a few southern waters such as Wedge Pond.

name: Mountain whitefish
note: Common in larger rivers. Good winter fishery on some open sections.

name: Lake trout
note: Native in Waterton and some northern lakes; present in a few big lakes and reservoirs (Spray, Abraham, Minnewanka).

name: Golden trout
note: Stocked in 1959 into a handful of high Castle-area lakes. Backcountry only.

name: Cuttbow (hybrid)
note: Rainbow x cutthroat hybrids where stocked rainbows overlap native cutthroat. No official AB code; CTBW used here.

name: Yellowstone cutthroat trout
note: Historically stocked in some alpine lakes. No confirmed site in this dataset yet; check the Alberta stocking reports.

name: Rainbow trout
note: Widely stocked and naturalized south of the Athabasca drainage.

name: Brook trout
note: Lower-elevation lakes and streams. Often generous limits; check regs.
